security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, or benign temporary-directory handling. Confirmed risks include unpinned remote Kubernetes manifests and a downloaded Flux installer executed with sudo without integrity verification. The examples also expose credentials through terminal commands and enable automated pruning against a production path.

remediation.issue: The Flux example executes a downloaded installer with root privileges without cryptographic verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned package or release artifact, verify its checksum or signature, and avoid root execution when possible.

remediation.issue: Argo CD manifests are applied from a mutable stable branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each manifest to a reviewed release tag or commit and verify the artifact before applying it.

remediation.issue: The Argo CD example enables pruning and self-healing for a production path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a non-production path in examples and require an explicit approval gate before production pruning or synchronization.

remediation.issue: Setup examples print an admin password and pass a repository token through a command argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use secret prompts, environment-independent credential helpers, or protected secret references that avoid shell history and process arguments.

content.user_title: Build Secure GitOps Workflows with Argo CD and Flux
content.value_statement: Kubernetes delivery becomes risky when cluster state and deployment changes lack a controlled source of truth. This skill provides practical Argo CD and Flux workflow guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Argo CD and Flux installation and bootstrap workflows.
Proposes Git repository layouts for applications, infrastructure, environments, and controller resources.
Creates Argo CD Application and Flux source and Kustomization examples.
Configures synchronization, pruning, retries, health checks, and maintenance windows.
Outlines canary and blue-green delivery strategies.
Covers external secret references, sealed secrets, and common synchronization troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires valid Kubernetes cluster access, repository permissions, and installed command-line tools.
Uses placeholder names, URLs, namespaces, and policies that require environment-specific review.
Does not execute deployments, validate generated manifests, or confirm controller compatibility.
Some installation examples depend on mutable upstream resources and require stronger integrity controls.

use_cases.title: Establish a cluster delivery platform
use_cases.description: Design repository structure, controller setup, synchronization policies, and production approval boundaries.

use_cases.title: Onboard an application to GitOps
use_cases.description: Define application sources, deployment destinations, secret references, and staged promotion behavior.

use_cases.title: Review deployment controls
use_cases.description: Assess pruning, self-healing, retries, health checks, and operational safeguards before rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic GitOps setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a beginner GitOps plan for my Kubernetes cluster using [Argo CD or Flux]. List prerequisites, safe installation choices, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is introducing GitOps to one non-production cluster.

prompt_templates.title: Design a repository layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps repository for [applications], [environments], and [infrastructure]. Explain ownership, promotion flow, and where controller resources belong.
prompt_templates.scenario: A platform team needs a maintainable repository structure.

prompt_templates.title: Configure application reconciliation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an Argo CD or Flux reconciliation design for [application]. Include sync intervals, retries, health checks, pruning safeguards, and secret references.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application team is moving an existing service to automated delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Architect controlled multi-cluster delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-cluster GitOps workflow for [environments]. Include progressive delivery, approval gates, rollback, RBAC, observability, and supply-chain integrity requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: An organization needs governed production delivery across several clusters.

output_examples.input: Plan Argo CD adoption for a staging cluster and one application.
output_examples.output: The plan separates controller installation, repository onboarding, staging synchronization, health validation, and rollback testing. Production automation remains disabled.

output_examples.input: Recommend safe synchronization behavior for production.
output: Disable automatic pruning until recovery tests pass.
Define maintenance windows and retry limits.
Alert on drift, failed health checks, and reconciliation errors.

output_examples.input: Compare Argo CD and Flux for a platform team.
output_examples.output: The comparison covers operating model, repository integration, reconciliation resources, access controls, multi-cluster patterns, and team maintenance requirements.

best_practices: Pin installation artifacts and verify checksums or signatures before applying them.
Test synchronization, pruning, rollback, and secret handling in staging before production.
Require least-privilege access, production approvals, health checks, and reconciliation alerts.
anti_patterns: Do not apply mutable remote manifests directly to a production cluster.
Do not store plaintext credentials in Git, command arguments, or shared terminal logs.
Do not enable automatic production pruning without tested recovery and explicit approval controls.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but deployment requires your tools, credentials, permissions, and explicit execution.

faq.question: Which GitOps controllers are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Argo CD and Flux installation, application sources, reconciliation, synchronization policies, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Can I use the examples unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders and review namespaces, repositories, permissions, versions, policies, and controller compatibility.

faq.question: How should production synchronization be protected?
faq.answer: Use approval gates, maintenance windows, least privilege, tested rollback, health checks, alerts, and cautious pruning settings.

faq.question: How are secrets handled?
faq.answer: The guidance favors External Secrets or sealed secrets. Keep plaintext values outside Git, shell history, logs, and command arguments.

faq.question: Does the skill support multi-cluster delivery?
faq.answer: It describes repository and controller patterns that can support multiple clusters. Each environment still requires tailored access and policy design.
